prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on what you want to do in Branson.

- If your priority is convenience to shows and restaurants and minimal driving, stay in a hotel on/near the 76 “Strip” or downtown (easy walk to theaters).
- If you want lake access, privacy, grilling/room for a group, or to relax in the Ozarks, an Airbnb (lake house or cabin) is usually better.
- If you want resort amenities (spa, restaurants, activities) with supportive service, choose a resort/hotel.

Below are specific, reliable choices by travel style + practical booking tips.

Best if you want to be close to shows and attractions (convenience)
- Hilton Branson Convention Center — central location, good for walking to shows, comfortable rooms and convention-space amenities.
- Radisson Hotel Branson (on/near 76 Country Blvd) — solid midrange option right on the Strip.
- Best Western Music Capital Inn — budget-friendly, family-oriented, convenient to attractions.

Best lakeside or upscale resort experience
- Chateau on the Lake (a Wyndham Grand) — true lakeside resort on Table Rock Lake with upscale rooms, spa and on-site dining.
- Big Cedar Lodge (near Ridgedale/just south of Branson) — high-end cabins and lodges with extensive outdoor activities, golf and family programming.
- Westgate Branson Woods Resort — condo-style units, family-friendly resort amenities.

Best for a unique/local stay / educational touch
- Keeter Center at College of the Ozarks — a well-regarded, slightly different lodging option (student-staffed service, quality dining, quiet campus setting).

Best for families or larger groups (Airbnb often wins)
- Search for Table Rock Lake waterfront homes (Indian Point, Hollister, Branson West) — many have private docks, multiple bedrooms, kitchens and outdoor space.
- Look for Ozark cabins near dogwood/tree-covered hills if you want hiking and privacy.

When an Airbnb makes the most sense
- You need a full kitchen, living space, multiple bedrooms, or a private dock for a boat.
- You’re traveling with a group/family and want cost per person to be lower.
- You prefer a quieter, more private setting away from the Strip.

When a hotel makes the most sense
- Short stay where you’ll mostly be at shows and attractions.
- You want on-site restaurants, daily housekeeping, concierge help, or to avoid cleaning/cancellation uncertainties.
- You want consistent service and easier late arrivals.

How to pick the right Airbnb or hotel
- For Airbnbs: favor Superhosts, read recent reviews (last 60–90 days), confirm parking and boat/dock permissions, check cleaning fee and cancellation policy, verify number of beds vs. guests, and ask about A/C and internet if you’ll be working.
- For hotels: compare location relative to the shows you’ll attend (many shows cluster on 76 Country Blvd), check free parking, and verify resort fees or extra charges.
- Book early for spring, summer and fall weekends (Branson is busy on concert/show weekends and school breaks).

Typical budgets (approximate)
- Budget/midrange hotels: $80–$160/night (depends on season)
- Upscale resorts: $180–$400+/night
- Airbnbs: vary widely — small cabins $80–$150; larger lakefront homes $200–600+ (weekends/holiday rates spike)

If you tell me:
- dates, number of people, kids/pets, and whether you want lake access vs. nightlife/strip convenience,
I’ll recommend 3–5 specific hotel rooms or active Airbnb listings that match your needs and price range.
